slides.heading: Japanese Encephalitis (JE)
slides.subtitle: A mosquito-borne viral brain infection transmitted by Culex mosquitoes.

slides.heading: Overview
bullets: Diagnosis: IgG and IgM antibodies, ELISA, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis.

slides.heading: Disease Course
bullets: <1% develop encephalitis: disorientation, weakness, coma; seizures common in children.
Classic sign: parkinsonian syndrome with mask-like facies, tremor, cogwheel rigidity, choreoathetoid movements.
Can cause acute flaccid paralysis resembling poliomyelitis.

slides.heading: Treatment (Hospital Admission)
bullets: Admit for altered mental status, seizures, high fever, neurologic signs.
Monitor vital signs, oxygen, neurologic function; fever control with paracetamol.
Anticonvulsants (diazepam, phenytoin) for seizures; IV fluids and nutrition.
Brain swelling: elevate head of bed, reduce stimulation, watch for herniation.

slides.heading: Key Takeaways
bullets: JE = Culex-borne viral encephalitis; incubation 5–15 days.
Hallmark: parkinsonian features (mask-like facies, cogwheel rigidity).
Most cases mild; <1% progress to severe encephalitis (seizures, coma).
No specific cure — supportive hospital care, anticonvulsants, ICP management.
